answers.implementation_then_now: There is no direct practice evidence on revocation after job loss in either period. Both law firm commentary (2022) and SERMIG's own guidance describe the Decreto 177 permit as no longer tied to an employment contract, and no documented pattern of revocation for job loss was found. The rating stays the same for 2023 and 2026, with low confidence.

SERMIG: Extranjeros que desarrollan actividades lícitas remuneradas

answers.sourcing_note: The LeyChile version metadata was read for 2022-12-31 (original text, 12-FEB-2022 to 06-AGO-2023) and for 2025-12-31 (intermediate version, 01-APR-2025 to 01-JUN-2026). The amending acts 21.589, 21.590, 21.610 and 21.655 were read; the clause of 21.730 touching Ley 21.325 was not. Decreto 177 shows a single version ('Única - 14-MAY-2022'), but the text of its Art. 21 could not be rendered.
answers.starting_answer_concern: Art. 72 of Ley 21.325 only sets the validity of the permit and does not itself protect status after job loss; the protection comes from Decreto 177. Extending a work-based permit reportedly requires proof of continued remunerated activity (about 60% of the permit period), so job loss can affect renewal. The MRD's rating 'Effectively Always; Sometimes' is not an allowed option and has been mapped to 'Usually; Effectively Always'.
answers.notes: Ley 21.816 (02-JUN-2026) amended Ley 21.325 after the window and is not considered here.

answers.implementation_then_now: Around 2023 the pathway worked, but with a large backlog. SERMIG granted 93,989 residencias definitivas in 2022, the highest figure in 20 years, while about 305,000 applications were pending and some had waited for years (La Tercera, May 2023; DF, 2023). By July 2025 SERMIG reported that the Rezago programme had resolved 99.4% of the inherited backlog and that more than 429,000 temporary and permanent applications were decided in 2024 to Q1 2025. Delays in 2023 were real, but the route was being used at scale in both periods. 'Usually' is kept for both dates; access improved but not enough to change the level.

practice_sources.title: La cifra más alta en 20 años: Migraciones entregó más de 94 mil residencias definitivas en 2022
Migraciones apuesta por resolver rezago de 305 mil solicitudes de residencias
Director Nacional de Migraciones realizó Cuenta Pública (2025)

answers.sourcing_note: Version metadata for both dates and the amending acts were read; the Ley 21.730 clause was not. Arts. 70, 72, 78 and 79 were read in the current consolidated text, which matches the 2021 enactment. The practice data come from SERMIG statements and press reports, not from independent audits.
answers.starting_answer_concern: Art. 55 of Ley 21.325 concerns the border-zone document and is not relevant. The operative provisions are Art. 70's final paragraph, under which residencia definitiva is 'siempre admisible' for numerals 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, 10 and 12 (numeral 2 covers paid work), and Arts. 78-79 (24 months of temporary residence). Given the 2022-23 backlog, 'Sometimes; Usually' would also be defensible for 2023.
answers.notes: Search results mention 185,250 overdue temporary and permanent applications as of March 2026; this was not read and falls after the window.

answers.change_2023_2026: There have been no right protections neither in 2023 nor in 2026

answers.implementation_then_now: Does not apply: in both periods, access to residencia definitiva depends on the subcategory. Art. 78 allows it only for a temporary permit 'que expresamente admita postular a ella'. Art. 70 guarantees admissibility only for listed subcategories, and seasonal workers (numeral 4) are not among them.
answers.sourcing_note: The current text of Art. 70 and Art. 78 was read, and the version metadata for both dates confirms no amendment. Ley 21.589, 21.590 and 21.610 also amended Ley 21.325 in 2023 but touched only arts. 5, 100, 132, 134, 147 and 166.
answers.starting_answer_concern: The starting citation says the 'temporary migrant workers' visa' does not allow an application for permanent status. That is inaccurate for the paid-work subcategory (Art. 70 No. 2), which is always admissible. The 'No' answer still holds because of seasonal workers (No. 4) and other subcategories.
answers.notes: Arts. 70 and 78 are quoted from the current consolidated text.

answers.implementation_then_now: Migrant workers use the Dirección del Trabajo (DT) redress channel at scale. In 2022, foreign workers filed 7,264 complaints and 22,304 claims, leading to more than 5,000 inspections and 2,449 sanctions. 15.2% of the sanctions were for breaches of contract provisions (El Desconcierto, citing a DT report, March 2023). The DT's stated inspection criterion is to enforce labour rights regardless of residence status (DT, May 2022). For 2025 the DT published a dedicated annual report on complaints and claims by foreign workers, showing the channel still operating; its PDF could not be read. There is no evidence of a shift.

answers.sourcing_note: Arts. 13 and 14 of Ley 21.325 were read in the current text ('Los extranjeros gozarán de los mismos derechos en materia laboral que los chilenos'), with version metadata for both dates. The text and version history of Código del Trabajo Art. 1 could not be rendered. The practice evidence for 2023-2026 is thinner: only the listing of the DT 2025 report was seen.
answers.notes: Art. 14(2) of Ley 21.325 obliges employers to meet labour obligations even when the worker's status is irregular, so redress reaches irregular workers as well.
